title: Water diffusion in biopolymer films
subtitle: Lesson summary · Fick's laws and how fillers slow water down

sections.title: Key idea
points: Water moves from high to low concentration.
The rate is set by the diffusion coefficient D (m²/s).
Thicker films take longer: t½ grows with L².

sections.title: Measuring uptake
steps: Dry the film to constant mass
Plot Mt/M∞ vs √t and fit D

sections.title: Common mistakes
points: Using wet thickness instead of dry thickness.
Fitting beyond Mt/M∞ ≈ 0.6 with the short-time equation.
Calling n = 0.45 'Fickian' for a cylinder or sphere without checking geometry.

takeaway: Well-dispersed platelets or rods make the water path longer, so D drops; agglomerates waste that effect.
source: Crank, The Mathematics of Diffusion (2nd ed., 1975); Ritger & Peppas, J. Control. Release 5 (1987) 23–36
